title: Requirements plane v0.1 (ADR-015)
description: Forge-native schema for generative intent. This is the one plane where Forge mints rather than adopts, because the authoring community — product and application teams writing specs for generation — is converging on a practice with no ratified DSL. The schema is versioned and migration-ready: when spec-driven development ratifies a language, the plane migrates and the graph does not.

requirements_schema.description: Reader dispatch key. An unknown version MUST raise, never fall back to the newest known reader — a reader defaulting to the wrong branch silently misreads valid documents, and the failure surfaces as nonsense findings rather than as a parse error (MP-02).

node_class.description: Requirements author intent; they are never reference vocabulary.

plane.description: Required with no default, per MP-08. A silent fallback would land requirements nodes in the architecture plane invisibly.

then.description: An internal non-human actor MUST resolve to an accountability anchor. Autonomy lives in the execution; accountability never leaves the human (ADR-010).

kind.description: Agents are actors. The anchor chain still terminates in a person: a non-human actor may hold `associated_with` and never `accountable_for` (ADR-010 §6a).

anchor_ref.description: The accountability anchor this actor is associated with. Optional for external human actors; required for internal system/agent actors. Never asserts accountability — the application registry is the sole system of record for that.

then.description: A ratified requirement without acceptance is prose. Acceptance is what makes it executable, and executability is the whole claim.

acceptance.description: Gherkin, embedded rather than reinvented — the one part of this space with a real standard is adopted verbatim. Projects directly into test skeletons.

realizes.description: Authored artifacts this requirement begat. The generative sibling of `governs`: `governs` points down the authority chain, `realizes` points forward through generation.

assertions.description: Properties the instantiated system must hold, never the platform that provides them: `compute_type: isolated_ephemeral`, not `runtime: lambda`. The graph must not change when a deployment technology does.

target_state.description: NOTE: there is deliberately no `realized_by` property. It is derived on read from inbound `realizes` edges (see intake_requirements.realized_by). Stored, it would enter the node's content digest, so generating an artifact would mutate the intent it was generated from and REQUIREMENTS_NEWER_THAN_CODE would compare against a value that moves every time code is generated.
